item: R3 item 5b (revised): pooling check and fold-count stability
status: post hoc relative to the paper's original precommit; written and committed before Step B runs

data.dataset: Camelyon17 (WILDS), 30 training slides from 3 training hospitals (10 each)
data.id_eval: id_val patches of the 30 training slides
data.ood: hospital-2 test patches (Track A primary OOD set)

step_A.inputs: cached Track A per-image scores outputs/rigor_pack/miccai_campaign/scores/camelyon_{fm}[_s43|_s44].npz (H11c 2-fold fits, fold seed = model seed); no refits

estimates.F1: mean over folds f of AUROC(id_val of fold 1-f scored by fit f, OOD scored by fit f)
estimates.F2_naive: Track E pooling: all id_val patches, each scored by the fit that did not see its slide, against OOD scores averaged over the two fits; one AUROC
estimates.F2_matched: each id_val patch compared with the OOD scores of the same fit that scored it; per-arm AUROC pooled with weights n_k (number of ID patches in the arm)

step_A.also_reported: F2_naive - F1, F2_matched - F1 per cell; s.d. of single-fit OOD scores (fit 0, fit 1) vs fit-averaged OOD scores
step_A.expectation_not_gate: F2_matched - F1 ~ 0 (fold-weight differences only); if F2_naive - F1 carries the gap, the mechanism is the averaging of OOD scores
step_A.verdict_rule: naive pooling explains the Maha gap if, in each of the three failing Mahalanobis cells at seed 42 (dinov2_vitb14, dinov2_vitl14, conch_v1_5), |F2_matched - F1| <= 0.02 while |F2_naive - F1| > 0.02; otherwise the gap persists under matched pooling

step_B.question: does a scorer fitted on (K-1)/K of the training slides approximate the scorer fitted on all of them?
step_B.folds: over the 30 training slides, stratified within hospital: per hospital the slides are sorted, shuffled with numpy default_rng([20261008, K]) and dealt round-robin into the K folds (counter continues across hospitals); one fold assignment per K
step_B.estimate: X_K = correctly (matched) pooled cross-fit AUROC = crossfit_ood.crossfit_auroc(protocol='default', fold_ids = fold of each id_val patch's slide); fit k uses all training patches of slides outside fold k and scores the id_val patches of fold k and all OOD patches; arms pooled with weights n_k

scorers.Mahalanobis: mahalanobis_l2 (Ledoit-Wolf on L2-normalised features, Track A definition)

step_B.features: R3 item-1 inputs camelyon_{fm}_s42.npz (FM features do not depend on the seed)
step_B.also_reported: leaky AUROC (scorer fitted on all 30 slides = deployed scorer), fit-set size per fold (min / mean / max patches), n_groups_fit, K, d, probe ID accuracy
step_B.uncertainty: point estimates for every cell first; then jackknife 95% CI (crossfit_ood, Busing weighted, blocks = slides) where affordable within the 1-day budget (Mahalanobis on CPU; kNN only with the GPU knn_mean_cosine scorer if it passes the R3 equality check, else no CI). Cells without a CI are reported as point estimates and marked so. CIs do not enter the criteria.
step_B.stability_criterion: |X_5 - X_10| <= 0.01 on >= 4 of 5 FMs, separately for Mahalanobis and for kNN; stable only if both pass
step_B.report_only_not_gate: |X_2 - X_5| per FM x scorer (distance of the paper's K = 2 numbers from the recommended setting)

decides.A_naive_explains: paper states cross-fitting = group-disjoint evaluation keeping every ID sample; warns naive pooling inflates AUROC (by up to the observed Maha gap); package implements matched pooling
decides.A_gap_persists: report as unexplained; recommend group-disjoint evaluation for Mahalanobis
decides.B_stable: K = 5 becomes the package default and the paper recommends it
decides.B_not_stable: recommend the largest affordable K and report the drift

stopping_rule: no new estimators, shrinkage tuning or alternative pooling schemes beyond naive and matched; report and stop
